item.title: HTML5 print mode emits "page 1" even without TOC

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use config `testing/myconfig_html5.json` with `html5.mode : "print"` and run: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Open `testing/lowlands-debug.html` and inspect generated CSS @page rules.
Observe `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` and visible page-number output (e.g. page 1), even when no TOC section is present.

item.expected-result: When TOC is not involved, page-number rendering should be controllable and not appear unexpectedly; users should be able to disable footer page numbers in HTML5 print mode without custom CSS surgery.

analysis.hypothesis: The output is generated in paged mode (`body.chordpro-paged`) because `html5.mode` is set to `print` in the active config. In paged mode, @page margin boxes are always generated from PDF format rules.

`lib/ChordPro/Output/HTML5Helper/FormatGenerator.pm` translates `%{page}` to `counter(page)` for footer slots. The effective default PDF format includes a footer page marker, producing `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` in generated CSS.

The page number is not TOC-driven in this reproduction. TOC-specific selectors only suppress page numbers on `@page toc`, but no TOC block is required for default page footer counters to appear on song pages.
analysis.root-cause: HTML5 print mode unconditionally inherits PDF format footer semantics for page margin boxes. Because default/effective PDF format contains `%{page}`, the generated CSS includes `counter(page)` and renders page numbers even in no-TOC songbooks.

tasks.task: Add explicit HTML5 print config switch to disable page counters independent of TOC (e.g., `html5.paged.page-numbers: false` or equivalent) and thread it into CSS generation.
Implement conditional suppression in FormatGenerator/layout pipeline so default footer page counters are omitted when the new switch is false.
Verify TOC-specific behavior remains intact (`@page toc` suppression and TOC target-counter rendering unaffected).

Alternative implementation path: document and support a config-only override via `pdf.formats.default.footer` with empty page slot for HTML5 print, without code changes; evaluate if sufficient UX-wise.
Add mirrored regression assertions for generated CSS (`counter(page)` present/absent according to switch or format override) in both HTML5 bugfix suites.

test.description: Generate HTML5 print output with page numbers disabled and verify no default footer `counter(page)` appears for song pages.
test.assertions: No `@bottom-right { content: counter(page); }` rule is emitted when disable switch/override is active.

test.description: Mirror the page-number suppression assertion and ensure TOC page targeting still works when TOC exists.
test.assertions: TOC counters remain functional; only unwanted default page footer counter is suppressed.

test.description: Run `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html` with the chosen option and inspect output in browser.

item.title: Full-Grid-SVG: Taktstriche zwischen Chord- und `|s`-Zeilen driften; `dn~up`-Paare sind optisch zu weit

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/lowlands.cho` and generate HTML5: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Inspect grid blocks containing `|s` lines with connected strums like `dn~up` (e.g. the first grid section).
Compare barline x-positions between chord row and strum row and inspect visual distance of connected `dn~up` arrows.
Observe that barlines are not consistently stacked and connected `dn~up` arrows appear too far apart (not “eng beieinander”).

item.expected-result: In full-grid SVG rendering, barlines in chord and `|s` rows must be vertically aligned at identical x-anchors. Connected `dn~up` pairs should be rendered as tight visual pairs (explicitly tighter than current rendering), matching the requested HTML5 style even if it differs from PDF spacing behavior.

analysis.hypothesis: `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm::grid_block_svg` computes positions row-locally (`my $column = 1;` per row and `x = (column - 0.5) * cell_width`). When strum rows expand tokens via `~` (e.g., `dn~up`), column progression diverges from chord rows and barline anchors drift between rows.

Connected `dn~up` rendering uses full-cell centers for both arrows and only adds a midline connector (`last_arrow_x + 2.8` to `x - 2.8`), so pair distance is dominated by full cell width and appears too wide for the requested “eng” style.

The current unified full-grid SVG path in HTML5 (`render_grid_block_svg` -> `grid_block_svg`) does not maintain a shared canonical beat/bar anchor model across rows; it relies on per-row token expansion, which is fragile for mixed chord/strum density.
analysis.root-cause: The full-grid SVG renderer lacks a shared row-independent geometry contract for beat/bar anchors and uses row-local token expansion, causing cross-row bar drift; additionally, connected strum pairs are spaced by full cell centers instead of compact pair geometry.

tasks.task: Introduce canonical shared x-anchors for bars/beats across all rows in `grid_block_svg`, independent of row-local token expansion.
Map strum `~`-connected pairs (`dn~up`, `up~dn`) to compact intra-beat pair geometry so arrows are visually tight.
Keep existing non-connected strum and bar/repeat semantics stable while applying compact pair spacing only to explicit connected pairs.
Add mirrored regression checks for (a) barline cross-row alignment and (b) bounded connector/pair spacing for connected `dn~up` segments.
Run focused HTML5 grid/strum suites and verify no regressions in standalone strum sections and previous full-grid fixes.

test.description: Validate barline x-anchor parity between chord and strum rows in decoded full-grid SVG payload.
test.assertions: Comparable barline nodes in paired rows share the same x positions within a narrow tolerance.
Connector span and arrow-pair spacing for connected pairs remain below an agreed compact threshold and are tighter than current baseline behavior.
Mirrored suite enforces identical full-grid spacing/alignment contract.

test.description: Regenerate `testing/lowlands-debug.html` and visually inspect first grid block with `dn~up` patterns.
test.assertions: Barlines are stacked between chord/strum rows and connected arrows appear tightly grouped.

r.observations: `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm::grid_block_svg` now derives canonical bar columns once and reuses them across all rendered rows, keeping chord and `|s` barlines vertically aligned even when row-local token expansion differs. Connected strum symbols in `class=chords` rows (`dn~up` / `up~dn`) now use compact intra-pair x-spacing (`tight_pair_step`) instead of full-cell center spacing, producing visibly tighter pairs. item.title: HTML5 Strum-SVG: Pfeil-Token entsprechen nicht der Tabelle aus Directives-env_grid (inkl. `us/ds`, `dx+`, `ua+`)

steps-to-reproduce.step: Use `testing/lowlands.cho` and generate HTML5: `perl script/chordpro.pl testing/lowlands.cho --generate=HTML5 --config=testing/myconfig_html5.json --output=testing/lowlands-debug.html`.
Open `docs/content/Directives-env_grid.md` (Strums table) and list token families (`u/up`, `dn/d`, `u+`, `d+`, `ua`, `da`, `ua+`, `da+`, `ux`, `dx`, `ux+`, `dx+`, `us`, `ds`, `us+`, `ds+`).
Inspect generated strum SVG semantics (full-grid path and standalone strum path), especially with mixed tokens like `d+~u+`, `~da`, `~ua`, `dx+`, `us`, `ds+`.

Observe mismatches against documentation semantics: several affix variants are not normalized consistently, and some documented families (notably staccato `us/ds`) are not represented as first-class strum variants in the current classifier/renderer contract.

item.expected-result: HTML5 strum rendering must match the documented token table semantics in `docs/content/Directives-env_grid.md` for all listed strum pseudo-chords. Equivalent forms must normalize identically (prefix/suffix and mixed modifiers), and rendered arrows/markers must remain stable and connected to intended beat/chord anchors.

analysis.hypothesis: `lib/ChordPro/Delegate/Strum.pm::strum_symbol_info` is currently prefix-biased (`^x`, `^+`, `^a`) with limited direction inference. This drops or misclassifies valid documented forms where modifiers appear in other positions (e.g., `d+`, `u+`, `da`, `ua`, `dx+`, `ua+`).

When classification fails, `grid_block_svg` / `strumline_svg` skip or degrade arrow rendering for those cells; connector behavior (`~`) then operates on incomplete anchors, producing perceived desync or unconnected arrow pairs.

Documentation defines additional families (including staccato `us/ds` and their accented variants) that are not explicitly modeled as first-class semantic flags in the current strum symbol contract, so full table parity is currently not guaranteed.
analysis.root-cause: Strum token normalization/classification in `ChordPro::Delegate::Strum` is incomplete relative to the documented token matrix: modifier order is not canonicalized robustly and not all documented families are represented as explicit render semantics.

tasks.task: Introduce canonical token parser in `strum_symbol_info` that normalizes documented token families independent of affix order (`+`, `a`, `x`, `s` around `u/d/up/dn`).

Add explicit semantic flags for documented families (normal, accent, arpeggio, arpeggio-accent, muted, muted-accent, staccato, staccato-accent) and keep backward compatibility for existing accepted forms.
Map normalized semantics to deterministic SVG markers in `grid_block_svg` and `strumline_svg` so token meaning remains visible and stable in both full-grid and standalone strum render paths.
Re-check `~` connector behavior after normalization to ensure connected pairs remain compact and anchored for mixed modifier tokens.
Add mirrored regression matrix covering the documented table tokens from `Directives-env_grid.md`, including suffix/prefix equivalence assertions (`+d` ≡ `d+`, `ad` ≡ `da`, etc.).
Run focused HTML5 strum/grid suites to confirm no regression in fixes from items 56–60.
